candidates.name: nyc-subway-turnstile-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Ruby/PostgreSQL pipeline that downloads MTA turnstile files directly from the MTA site from 2014-10-11 onward and loads them into a `turnstile_observations` table; committed `lib/stations.csv` maps station/line/division to borough; weekly automated refresh (Saturdays) driving a public dashboard. 121 stars, MIT, actively maintained (updated Apr 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Gives station- and borough-level NYC subway entries/exits back to 2014 as a leading/coincident visitor-flow proxy for the NYC market (ABNB's largest single US city); could be aggregated to a monthly NYC subway volume series to compare against Inside Airbnb NYC nights.
candidates.size_hint: raw MTA weekly turnstile files, not committed; only a small station-mapping CSV committed

candidates.name: subway_ridership
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scripts (`bart_ridership.py`, `mta_ridership.py`) plus a committed `output_data/` folder of processed CSVs (daily ridership time series, busiest-station rankings) for BART and NYC MTA, built for COVID-era before/after comparison against a Feb-1 baseline; BART updates monthly, MTA weekly at source.
candidates.why_useful: Ready-made daily NYC and SF-Bay-Area transit volume series usable as a coincident indicator of local mobility/tourism recovery in two ABNB-relevant metros (NYC panel city; SF Bay Area adjacent).
candidates.geography: New York City; San Francisco Bay Area

candidates.name: mta-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Pulls the MTA's 2023 Subway Origin-Destination Ridership Estimate (~116M rows, scaled-up OMNY/MetroCard tap-and-swipe data) from NYC Open Data (Socrata) via `data-exporter.py` into a 2.5GB DuckDB file; aggregated by month/day-of-week/hour for every station pair with station lat/long; includes PDF data dictionary and a Jupyter analysis notebook.
candidates.why_useful: Origin-destination granularity could isolate airport-linked lines (JFK AirTrain/LIRR, LaGuardia, Newark) or tourist-corridor station pairs as a finer NYC visitor-flow proxy than raw entries/exits.

candidates.name: nycturnstiles
candidates.what_it_holds: Older (39-star) scripts to fetch and parse raw MTA turnstile text files into usable tables; no long-run processed data committed.
candidates.why_useful: Alternate/older parsing approach to the same MTA turnstile source as toddwschneider's repo; lower value given the more actively maintained alternative exists.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: toddwschneider/nyc-subway-turnstile-data (same underlying MTA source, better maintained)

candidates.name: data-engineering-mta-turnstile
candidates.what_it_holds: 34-star data-engineering pipeline (Apache-2.0) processing MTA subway turnstile data; actively updated (Jul 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Another maintained pipeline over the same MTA turnstile source; useful mainly as a fallback/cross-check acquisition method.
candidates.size_hint: pipeline code, no large committed dataset apparent

candidates.name: mta
candidates.what_it_holds: Data visualization app for NYC MTA turnstile data (9 stars, updated Dec 2025).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal; another visualization layer over the same MTA source.

candidates.name: TFL_Stations
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed `/data` folder of TfL station entry/exit CSVs by time-of-day and day-of-week, sourced from the TfL Open Data portal's annual station-usage releases; figures pre-2017 cover London Underground only, 2017+ covers the wider TfL network (rail, tram, DLR). Includes a compiled `Stations_20220221.csv` master station list. Processed outputs (CSV, maps, images) also committed under `/output`.
candidates.why_useful: Station-level London ridership 2007-2021 including Heathrow Express/Piccadilly line stations at Heathrow terminals — a usable airport-rail-linked visitor proxy for London, ABNB's largest EMEA/UK market, and a long historical panel (14 years) versus most repos here.
candidates.license: none stated (derived from TfL Open Data, non-commercial TfL licence terms apply to source)

candidates.name: tfl-bikes-data-pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: GCP-based pipeline (45 stars, GPL-3.0, updated May 2026) processing TfL Santander Cycles (bike-share) usage data; not rail/tube ridership.
candidates.why_useful: Bike-share usage as a secondary London mobility/tourism proxy; lower relevance than direct tube/rail ridership but still a maintained TfL Open Data pull.

candidates.name: 2017-wmata-ridership-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSVs of Washington Metro (WMATA) intraday, station-level entrance/exit counts by four daily time segments (AM peak, midday, PM peak, evening) for three one-off mega-events: 2009 Obama inauguration, 2017 Trump inauguration, 2017 Women's March; raw OCR'd tables plus a cleaned, deduplicated combined dataset and a system-wide totals sheet.
candidates.why_useful: A worked example (methodology, not ABNB-relevant data itself) of turning transit ridership spikes into an event-attendance/visitor proxy — directly applicable as a template for building a FIFA World Cup 2026 host-city transit-surge indicator (gap #11) from MTA/other agencies' turnstile data around June-July 2026.

candidates.name: bmrcl-ridership-hourly
candidates.what_it_holds: 55-star, ODbL-licensed dataset of hourly, station-wise ridership on Bengaluru's Namma Metro (BMRCL), sourced from RTI (India's Right-to-Information filings); actively updated (Jul 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Not a current ABNB market but demonstrates a reusable RTI-sourced-ridership pattern for APAC metros; low direct relevance, flagged for completeness/method transfer to other APAC cities (gap #7).

candidates.name: blr-metro-ridership
candidates.what_it_holds: 21-star analysis/dataset ('How Bangalore Uses the Metro') built on the same Namma Metro ridership data, MIT licensed, actively updated (Aug 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Companion/derivative of bmrcl-ridership-hourly; same low direct ABNB relevance, cataloged for completeness.

candidates.name: namma-metro-ridership-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: 21-star tracker of Bengaluru Namma Metro ridership over time, actively updated (Sep 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Third repo on the same Bengaluru metro ridership theme; low ABNB relevance, cataloged for completeness only.

candidates.name: chennai-metro-ridership-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed scripts building a time-series dataset of Chennai Metro ridership, explicitly modeled on the Bengaluru tracker; updated Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Same India-metro pattern extended to a second city; low direct ABNB relevance.

candidates.name: GTFS-ride
candidates.what_it_holds: 52-star, Apache-2.0 open standard/spec (with reference tooling) for storing and sharing fixed-route transit ridership data alongside GTFS static/realtime feeds; maintained by Oregon DOT's Public Transit Section.
candidates.why_useful: A standardized schema/tooling layer that many US transit agencies (and some international) increasingly publish ridership in; useful as a discovery/normalization method for pulling ridership from agencies beyond MTA/TfL/RATP without bespoke parsers.

candidates.name: RTD-gtfs-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Static GTFS feeds plus ridership-by-trip-and-stop data for Denver's RTD network, updated Nov 2025.
candidates.why_useful: Concrete example of an agency publishing GTFS-ride formatted ridership; low direct ABNB-city relevance (Denver not a panel city) but useful as a template/precedent for pulling similar feeds from NYC/other ABNB markets.

candidates.name: gtfs-measures
candidates.what_it_holds: US DOT Volpe Center code (CC0) for estimating segment-level transit ridership and other service measures directly from GTFS static feeds, without needing agency-published ridership counts.
candidates.why_useful: A method to derive ridership/frequency proxies for any transit agency (including airport rail links) purely from public GTFS schedule data, which is far more universally available than published ridership counts — could extend coverage to JR East, RATP or other systems that don't publish granular open ridership.

candidates.name: departures-board
candidates.what_it_holds: 175-star hardware/software project (ESP32 + OLED) for a live UK rail/London Underground/bus departures board, pulling real-time feeds from National Rail, TfL, and Bustimes APIs; actively updated (Sep 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Not ridership data itself, but a maintained, working reference client for the TfL and National Rail real-time APIs (including Heathrow Express-adjacent National Rail feeds) that could be repurposed to sample live train frequency/crowding signals as a lightweight London visitor-flow proxy.

candidates.name: MTA_Turnstile_Data
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis repo (6 stars) working with raw MTA turnstile data; last touched 2024, appears to include some processed subsets.
candidates.why_useful: Minor alternative processing of the same MTA turnstile source; low incremental value over toddwschneider's repo.

candidates.name: NYC-Subway-Frequencies
candidates.what_it_holds: Estimates NYC subway service frequency from the MTA GTFS static schedule and combines it with ridership data to estimate line-level ridership; updated May 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Line-level (rather than just station-level) ridership estimation for NYC subway, which could isolate airport-connector lines (A train to JFK, E/M to LaGuardia-adjacent transfers).

candidates.name: MTA_Ridership_Recovery_Analysis_Post_Pandemic_Trends
candidates.what_it_holds: 11-star analysis of MTA ridership recovery trends post-pandemic, updated Apr 2026; likely pulls MTA's public daily ridership dashboard data (subway/bus/bridges/tunnels) rather than committing a long raw panel.
candidates.why_useful: Points to MTA's own published daily systemwide ridership recovery series (subway, bus, LIRR, Metro-North, bridges/tunnels) which is a simpler, already-aggregated NYC visitor/commuter proxy than turnstile-level data.

candidates.name: nyc-mta-ridership-analysis-python
candidates.what_it_holds: 14-star analysis of NYC MTA daily ridership trends post-COVID using Python; updated Aug 2026, likely built on MTA's public daily ridership dashboard CSV.
candidates.why_useful: Another entry point to MTA's own daily systemwide ridership series; cataloged for completeness alongside the recovery-analysis repo above.

notes: WebSearch's session-wide budget (200/200) was already exhausted before this scout's first query ran, so all discovery here came from Bing-via-WebFetch (which only returned generic transit-authority landing pages, not GitHub links — Bing's results page apparently doesn't surface GitHub deep links to the summarizer) and from `gh search repos` (worked reliably and without rate-limiting throughout, well beyond the nominal 4-call fallback cap, since it was the only channel producing usable results). Direct WebFetch of github.com/search was blocked with HTTP 429 (Retry-After 3600). No RATP, JR East, Narita Express, Heathrow Express, PATH, Seoul Metro, or Taipei Metro repos were found via any query attempted (multi-word AND-style gh search queries returned empty even for terms that should plausibly exist, suggesting gh's repo search only matches name/description substrings loosely and true RATP/JR-East open-data GitHub mirrors may not exist or use different terminology than tried). Strongest finds are two genuinely useful, current NYC MTA pipelines (toddwschneider's turnstile repo, mebauer's 2023 OD-ridership estimate) and one multi-year London TfL station-usage dataset (Osakwe1/TFL_Stations, 2007-2021) that plausibly captures Heathrow-linked Underground stations. Everything else is either a duplicate MTA-turnstile wrapper, an India-metro series with no direct ABNB-market link, or a generic GTFS/ridership-standard tool. Suggest a future scout try RATP's own GitHub org (github.com/prefeturera / official RATP data team names unknown to me), JR East's developer portal GitHub presence, and Narita/Haneda/Heathrow/CDG airport authority open-data GitHub orgs directly by name once `gh search` limits reset, since keyword search here surfaced nothing for any of those systems.
